indication.text: Treatment of babesiosis in dogs with clinical signs and/or demonstrated Babesia organisms in the blood.
indication.quote: For the treatment of babesiosis in dogs with clinical signs and/or demonstrated Babesia organisms in the blood.

dose_regimen.frequency: single injection, repeated in two weeks (total of two treatments)
dose_regimen.quote: IMIZOL® is to be administered at a rate of 6.6 mg/kg b.w. (3 mg/lb) (i.e. 0.25 mL/10 lb.). Repeat the dose in two weeks for a total of two treatments.

target_animal_safety.duration: two subcutaneous doses two weeks apart; clinical chemistry followed through Day 42
target_animal_safety.n_animals: ten per group (four Imizol dose groups plus one saline control group)

findings.finding: Pain on injection in nearly all dogs at every dose
findings.quote: Imizol® caused pain on injection in nearly all animals, regardless of dose.

findings.finding: Injection site swelling after the second injection: 4/10 at 2.2 mg/kg and all dogs at higher doses
findings.quote: Injection site reactions (swelling) after the second injection of Imizol were present in 4 out of the 10 dogs which received the lowest dose (2.2 mg/kg) and in all of the dogs which received the higher doses of Imizol.

findings.finding: One injection site ulceration at the highest dose (9.9 mg/kg), recurring after the second dose
findings.quote: One injection site reaction (ulceration of injection site) occurred at the highest dose (9.9 mg/kg).

findings.finding: Post-treatment vomiting in 1 to 4 of 10 dogs in every Imizol group, not dose related (cholinergic effect)
findings.quote: Post-treatment vomiting was seen in all Imizol-treated groups at a frequency of 1 to 4 out of 10 dogs. The adverse effect was not dose related nor did the dogs respond the same to both injections. These results are consistent with the cholinergic effects attributed to Imizol.

findings.finding: Statistically significant ALT and AST increases at 9.9 mg/kg on Days 21, 28 and 35, resolved by Day 42
findings.quote: On Days 21, 28 and 35 of the study there was a statistically significant increase in serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT, SGPT) and arginine aminotransferase (AST, SGOT) in the 9.9 mg/kg b.w. as compared to the placebo group. At Day 42, these differences were no longer apparent.

findings.finding: No effect at any dose on body temperature, body weight, hematology, other clinical chemistry or gross pathology; margin of safety at 6.6 mg/kg SC repeated in two weeks judged adequate
findings.quote: Imizol® had no effects, at any dose level, on body temperature, body weight, hematology, other clinical chemistry values or gross pathology. This study demonstrates that the margin of safety for Imizol® administered to dogs at 6.6 mg/kg b.w. subcutaneously and repeated in two weeks is adequate for its intended use.

findings.finding: 90-day oral tolerance study (5, 20 or 80 mg/kg daily): all four males died and two females euthanized in extremis at 80 mg/kg
findings.quote: In the 80 mg/kg group, all the male dogs(4) died during the trial and two of the females were euthanized in extremis. Their clinical signs included salivation, diarrhea, anorexia, dyspnea, tachycardia, listlessness and weakness.

findings.finding: Oral tolerance study: no toxicologically significant changes at 5 mg/kg; liver and intestines were the target organs
findings.quote: There were no changes of toxicological significance in the 5 mg/kg group as compared to controls. The target organs of toxicity were liver and intestines in this study of imidocarb using the oral route of administration.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Imizol was administered to four groups of ten, 9 month-old Beagle dogs at 2.2, 5.5, 7.7 or 9.9 mg/kg b.w. subcutaneously, given twice with two weeks between doses. A control group (ten similar animals) was administered saline in an identical manner.

effectiveness.design: Field trials: two published papers (Irwin 1991, Australia; Adeyanju 1982, Nigeria) and one 1996 U.S. multi-investigator clinical trial in pet dogs naturally infected with Babesia canis alone or with other hemoparasites; Imizol 4-5 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg IM or SC; 8 untreated puppies (Irwin 1991) served as controls (all died)
effectiveness.n_dogs: 325 treated (313 at 4 to 5 mg/kg plus twelve at 10 mg/kg)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Complete recovery or progressive remission of clinical signs (relapse and death also tabulated)
effectiveness.result: Complete recovery or progressive remission in 90% (294/325) of treated dogs; two 5 mg/kg dogs relapsed; seven dogs died of babesiosis despite 4-5 mg/kg; none of the 10 mg/kg dogs died; all eight untreated control puppies died; one dog accidentally overdosed at 24 mg/kg died of Imizol toxicity
effectiveness.quote: Imizol® was administered at a dose rate of 4 to 5 mg/kg b.w. by intramuscular or subcutaneous injection to a total of 313 dogs. Twelve dogs received 10 mg/kg b.w. Complete recovery or a progressive remission of clinical signs was reported in 90% (294/325) of the cases treated with either 4 to 5 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg of imidocarb.

adverse_reactions.term: Pain at injection and salivation (U.S. field trial)
adverse_reactions.quote: Pain at the time of injection and salivation were frequently reported by veterinarians in the United States.

adverse_reactions.term: Nasal drips, vomiting, panting, agitation, injection site swelling (transient; field trial)
adverse_reactions.quote: Other transient adverse effects reported were nasal drips, vomiting, panting, agitation, and injection site swelling.

adverse_reactions.term: Death from Imizol toxicity after accidental overdose (field trial)
adverse_reactions.quote: One (1) dog which received 24 mg/kg b.w. (accidental overdose) died of Imizol® toxicity.

adverse_reactions.treated: 1 to 4 out of 10 dogs per Imizol group
adverse_reactions.quote: Post-treatment vomiting was seen in all Imizol-treated groups at a frequency of 1 to 4 out of 10 dogs.

adverse_reactions.term: Injection site swelling after second injection (laboratory toxicity study)
adverse_reactions.treated: 4 out of 10 dogs at 2.2 mg/kg; all dogs at higher doses
adverse_reactions.quote: Injection site reactions (swelling) after the second injection of Imizol were present in 4 out of the 10 dogs which received the lowest dose (2.2 mg/kg) and in all of the dogs which received the higher doses of Imizol.

notes: Original NADA (1997). No PK parameters reported (an Abdullah 1984 IV 4 mg/kg study is cited only for adverse effects: 1 of 13 dogs died). Target animal safety dose_multiples are the actual SC doses tested; the summary does not express them as multiples of the 6.6 mg/kg label dose (9.9 mg/kg is 1.5x by arithmetic). Dose determination (93 dogs, 0-6 mg/kg; Guelfi 1980/1981, Euzeby 1981, Awaz 1984) and dose confirmation (1,031 dogs; Ogunkoya 1981 5 mg/kg SC, Bodade 1986 6 mg/kg IM) are literature summaries whose tables were flattened by PDF extraction and are not captured. Field-trial adverse reactions are reported qualitatively with no frequencies and no treated control group (the only controls were 8 untreated puppies). Summary General Information has no Species/Class field; species taken from the indication.

indication.text: Reduction of hyperglycemia and hyperglycemia-associated clinical signs in cats with diabetes mellitus.
indication.quote: PROZINC (protamine zinc recombinant human insulin) is indicated for the reduction of hyperglycemia and hyperglycemia-associated clinical signs in cats with diabetes mellitus.

dose_regimen.route: Subcutaneous (back of the neck or side of the cat, U-40 insulin syringe)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: given concurrently with or right after a meal; dose adjusted on clinical signs and glucose nadirs until adequate glycemic control (nadir 80-150 mg/dL on a 9-hour curve)
dose_regimen.quote: The initial recommended PROZINC dose is 0.1 - 0.3 IU insulin/pound of body weight (0.2 - 0.7 IU/kg) every 12 hours. The dose should be given concurrently with or right after a meal.

target_animal_safety.duration: 45 days (field study) and 136 days (extended use field study)

findings.finding: Hypoglycemia (blood glucose < 50 mg/dL) in seventy-one of the treated cats, mostly without clinical signs
findings.quote: Seventy-one cats experienced hypoglycemia (defined as a blood glucose value of < 50 mg/dL on the blood glucose curve).

findings.finding: One serious hypoglycemic event (stupor, recumbency, hypothermia, seizures) that resolved with supportive therapy
findings.quote: One cat had a serious hypoglycemic event associated with stupor, lateral recumbency, hypothermia and seizures. The cat fully recovered after supportive therapy and finished the study.

findings.finding: Seven cats euthanized during the 45-day study (one for hypoglycemia, two ketoacidosis, four for concurrent conditions)
findings.quote: Deaths: Seven cats were euthanized during the study. One was euthanized by the referring veterinarian for hypoglycemia. Two had ketoacidosis. Four cats were euthanized after receiving PROZINC for less than 1 week due to worsening of concurrent medical conditions.

findings.finding: No unusual clinical pathology changes Day 0 to Day 45
findings.quote: Serum chemistry and hematology results from blood samples collected on Day 0 were compared to those from Day 45. No unusual changes were seen.

findings.finding: Fourteen cats died or were euthanized in the extended use study; insulin continued despite anorexia/hypoglycemia contributed in two
findings.quote: Fourteen cats died or were euthanized during the extended use study. In two cases, continued use of insulin despite anorexia and signs of hypoglycemia contributed to the deaths.

findings.finding: Safety was based on the field studies; no laboratory margin-of-safety study
findings.quote: The safety of protamine zinc recombinant human insulin was confirmed in the field study and the extended use field study.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Adverse Reactions: In the field study, 176 cats received PROZINC insulin.

effectiveness.design: Multicenter (19 investigators), single-arm, open-label 45-day field study (IPI-PZI-0106) in client-owned diabetic cats; all cats received PROZINC and were compared with historically derived experience per 21 CFR 514.117(b)(4)(iv); 187 cats enrolled, 176 treated (safety population)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Treatment success at Day 45: improvement in at least one blood glucose variable (curve mean, nadir or fructosamine) and at least one clinical sign (polyuria, polydipsia, body weight); effective if lower bound of the 90% CI for success > 66%
effectiveness.result: 115/151 (76.2%) treatment successes, 90% CI 70.5% to 81.9%; six cats transiently diabetic and off insulin at study end
effectiveness.quote: Results: Of the 151 cats included in the effectiveness analysis, 115 (76.2%) were considered treatment successes. The 90% confidence interval was 70.5% to 81.9%.

adverse_reactions.quote: Vomiting 23 Lethargy 22 Diarrhea, loose stool 10 Cystitis, hematuria 6 Upper respiratory infection 3
Vomiting 23 Lethargy 22 Diarrhea, loose stool 10 Cystitis, hematuria 6 Upper respiratory infection 3
Vomiting 23 Lethargy 22 Diarrhea, loose stool 10 Cystitis, hematuria 6 Upper respiratory infection 3
Vomiting 23 Lethargy 22 Diarrhea, loose stool 10 Cystitis, hematuria 6 Upper respiratory infection 3
Seventy-one cats experienced hypoglycemia (defined as a blood glucose value of < 50 mg/dL on the blood glucose curve).
Injection site reactions: Three cats had injection site reactions.

notes: Species is CATS: this is the original NADA 141-297 approval (2009); the dog indication was added by the 2019 supplement (foi 6708). The n_dogs field holds the cat count. Adverse reaction counts are cases among 176 treated cats with no control group (single-arm design); the Table 5 row quote was flattened into one line by PDF extraction (column order: reaction, number of cases). Extended use study IPI-PZI-0206 (145 cats enrolled, 113 completed, 136 days; fructosamine and body weight continued to improve; 12 cats went into remission) not captured as a separate effectiveness entry. No PK data and no laboratory target animal safety study; TAS section relies on the field studies and literature.

indication.text: Reduction of hyperglycemia and hyperglycemia-associated clinical signs in dogs with diabetes mellitus (supplement adds dogs to the existing cat indication).
indication.quote: ProZinc® (protamine zinc recombinant human insulin) is indicated for the reduction of hyperglycemia and hyperglycemia-associated clinical signs in cats and dogs with diabetes mellitus.

dose_regimen.dose: starting dose 0.2-0.5 IU insulin/lb (0.5-1.0 IU/kg); naive dogs at the lower end, poorly controlled/transitioning dogs at the mid to higher end
dose_regimen.frequency: once daily (twice daily may be considered if duration of action is inadequate, each dose about 25% less than the once-daily dose)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: given with or right after a meal; titrated on clinical signs and blood glucose curve/fructosamine (adequate control: nadir 80-125 mg/dL, maximum <= 300 mg/dL)
dose_regimen.quote: The recommended starting dose for ProZinc® is 0.2-0.5 IU insulin/pound of body weight (0.5-1.0 IU/kg) once daily.

target_animal_safety.duration: up to 6 months (Day 182) in the field study

findings.finding: 80 hypoglycemic episodes: 37 with clinical signs in 24 dogs, 40 without signs in 27 dogs, 3 unknown in 2 dogs
findings.quote: Hypoglycemia: There were 80 hypoglycemic episodes recorded during the study; 37 episodes were associated with clinical signs in 24 dogs, 40 were without clinical signs in 27 dogs, and 3 were with unknown signs in 2 dogs.

findings.finding: Two dogs euthanized when hypoglycemia did not resolve with supportive care
findings.quote: Although most dogs recovered after supportive care (ranging from hospitalization and intravenous dextrose to oral glucose supplementation), two dogs were euthanized when the hypoglycemia did not resolve with supportive care.

findings.finding: Mean cholesterol elevated at Day 182 (432.6 mg/dL vs 333.7 mg/dL at Day -1); no other drug-related clinical pathology changes
findings.quote: Clinical pathology: Mean cholesterol was elevated at Day 182 (432.6 mg/dL, normal range 131-345 mg/dL) compared to Day -1 (333.7 mg/dL). No other clinically significant, potentially drug-related changes were seen in laboratory testing.

findings.finding: Injection site reactions in seven dogs, all resolved without stopping ProZinc
findings.quote: Injection site reactions: Seven dogs had injection site reactions, including observations of thickened skin, swelling, bumps at the injection site, and redness. All injection site reactions resolved without cessation of ProZinc® therapy.

findings.finding: Eleven dogs with diabetic ketoacidosis (four died/euthanized); twenty-one with pancreatitis
findings.quote: Eleven dogs were diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis. Four of these 11 dogs died or were euthanized, one after one dose of ProZinc®. Twenty-one dogs were diagnosed with pancreatitis.

findings.finding: 36 deaths/euthanasias, six possibly related to ProZinc
findings.quote: Deaths: Thirty-six (36) dogs died or were euthanized, six of which were possibly related to ProZinc®.

findings.finding: Safety confirmed in the field study including an extended use phase; no laboratory margin-of-safety study
findings.quote: The safety of ProZinc® was confirmed in the field study, which included an extended use phase.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: In the field study, 276 dogs received ProZinc® insulin daily for up to 6 months.

effectiveness.design: Pivotal multicenter (16 US sites), single-arm, open-label GCP field study (Study 2012028, 2013-2017) in client-owned diabetic dogs; ProZinc started at 0.5-1.0 IU/kg SC once daily and titrated to effect for up to 6 months; compared with historically derived experience per 21 CFR 514.117(b)(4)(iv); 276 dogs enrolled/treated (safety population), 224 evaluated for effectiveness
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Treatment success at Day 84: composite of improvement in at least one laboratory variable (blood glucose curve mean, nadir, or fructosamine) and at least one clinical sign (polyuria, polydipsia, or weight loss) vs baseline; effective if lower bound of the 95% CI >= 60%
effectiveness.result: 162/224 (72%) treatment successes; 95% CI 61.4 to 80.9% (lower bound above the 60% criterion)
effectiveness.quote: Results: Of the 224 dogs included in the effectiveness analysis, 162 (72%) were considered treatment successes. The 95% confidence interval was 61.4 to 80.9%.

adverse_reactions.quote: Anorexia (anorexia, decreased appetite, inappetence, and not eating) 28 (10.1%)

notes: Supplemental approval (2019) adding dogs to NADA 141-297. The pharmacokinetics entries are pharmacodynamic ranges (onset of action, time to glucose nadir, duration of action) from Table II.1 of PK/PD Study 2010062 (10 healthy fasted Beagles; 0.5 IU/kg n=5, 0.8 IU/kg single site n=10, 0.8 IU/kg divided over three sites n=6); no classical PK parameters (Cmax, AUC, half-life) are reported.
